Apple today celebrated the opening of its Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston, Texas. Here are the details.

Apple will train business leaders at its new Advanced Manufacturing Center in Houston

Apple today opened its new Advanced Manufacturing Center (AMC) in Houston. The center offers free training and educational courses for small and medium-sized businesses, giving them hands-on access to the latest equipment, interactive labs, and a range of tools to accelerate innovation. The AMC is housed at the same Houston facility responsible for producing and shipping Apple's advanced AI servers, and will begin producing Mac mini this year. [...] Apple CEO Tim Cook said: "In just nine months, we have invested hundreds of millions of dollars into this Houston facility. We have built the factory, started production, and shipped the first batch of advanced AI servers out the door. Today we are delighted to open the new Advanced Manufacturing Center, a place where businesses, workers, and students can learn the same innovative processes we use to build Apple's most groundbreaking products. We also look forward to commencing Mac mini production later this year. We believe in American workers and American ingenuity, and we are moving forward at a remarkable pace, because what we want to create is more than just great products—we want to build the future of American manufacturing."

Tim Cook said on social media that he made a special trip to Houston to attend the opening event. The opening ceremony was also attended by a number of government officials, including U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Houston Mayor John Whitmire, U.S. Representative Christian Menefee, Harris County Precinct One Commissioner Rodney Ellis, among others.

The AMC covers 20,000 square feet, and Apple experts will be on hand to "share their knowledge directly with participating businesses and entrepreneurs, helping accelerate the development of smart manufacturing in the United States."

The first cohort of business leaders arrived at the center today to take part in the inaugural training course. Today's curriculum focused on smart manufacturing technologies, including "machine learning-driven quality control and advanced automation."
